title: "Mamilla 1" Feasibility analysis of hyperspectral imaging for the assessment of nipple perfusion parameters in the early postpartum period under routine clinical conditions: an exploratory observational study
summary:
Breastfeeding provides substantial health benefits for both mothers and infants. However, many women experience nipple pain, redness, or nipple injury during the first days after birth. At present, these changes are mainly assessed by clinical examination and maternal symptoms. As local tissue changes may be associated with alterations in microcirculation and tissue perfusion, the objective assessment of perfusion-related tissue parameters may provide additional clinically relevant information. However, little is currently known about physiological nipple perfusion during the early postpartum period under routine clinical conditions.

The aim of this feasibility study is therefore to investigate whether perfusion-related tissue parameters of the nipple can be reliably acquired with sufficient data quality using non-contact hyperspectral imaging (HSI) under routine conditions on a mother–infant unit. Each participant will undergo a single HSI measurement during her inpatient stay. Data analysis will take into account the interval between the measurement and the most recent breastfeeding session, as well as the postpartum day. In addition, the study will evaluate the practical feasibility of integrating HSI into routine clinical care and the quality and analysability of the acquired data. The findings will provide the methodological basis for subsequent studies investigating physiological nipple perfusion dynamics and potential alterations associated with inflammatory or other pathological nipple conditions.
conditions: Physiological nipple perfusion during the early postpartum period and feasibility of hyperspectral imaging (HSI) for assessing perfusion-related tissue parameters.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•    Written informed consent 
•    Breastfeeding women in the early postpartum period receiving inpatient care at the University Women’s Hospital
•    Active breastfeeding according to the newborn’s needs
Exclusion criteria:
•    Expected noncompliance by the patient or the patient’s inability to understand the purpose of the clinical trial
•    Lack of patient consent
•    Acute systemic infections
•    Insufficient knowledge of German
